description: Transaction records that must be rejected, each with the reason.

cases.name: zero_amount
cases.why: amount is constrained to greater than zero. A zero transfer is not an event; admitting it would add a counterparty to every fan-in count for free.

cases.name: negative_amount
cases.why: Direction is carried by the sender and receiver columns, not by the sign of the amount. A negative amount would reverse a transfer without reversing its edge in the graph.

cases.name: missing_reference
cases.why: reference is required and unique. It is how a complaint naming a transaction is matched deterministically; without it the correlation drops to an inference tier.

cases.name: missing_occurred_at
cases.why: occurred_at is required. Every window, rate and velocity feature is defined over it, and a transfer with no time cannot be placed in any of them.

cases.name: currency_not_three_letters
cases.why: currency is a three-character code. 'Rs' would create a second currency bucket that looks like a typo and is impossible to reconcile later.

cases.name: unknown_channel
cases.why: channel is an enum. An unrecognised channel would be stored and then never match any channel-specific rule, which looks like the rule failing.

cases.name: unknown_sender_account
cases.why: Both account columns are foreign keys. An unknown sender must fail the batch rather than create a phantom account, which would appear in the graph as a node with no history.

cases.name: occurred_at_in_the_future
cases.why: A transfer dated beyond the clock-skew tolerance is a source-system error. Admitting it would let a future-dated row sit at the head of every recency window indefinitely.

cases.name: amount_not_numeric
cases.why: amount must parse as a decimal. A string that happens to contain separators is the most common real-world feed defect and the most dangerous to coerce silently.
